messages.content:
" *

Gets the type arguments of a class/interface based on a subtype. For * instance, this method will determine that both of the parameters for the * interface {@link Map} are {@link Object} for the subtype * {@link java.util.Properties Properties} even though the subtype does not * directly implement the Map interface.

This method * returns null if type is not assignable to * toClass. It returns an empty map if none of the classes or * interfaces in its inheritance hierarchy specify any type arguments.

*

A side-effect of this method is that it also retrieves the type * arguments for the classes and interfaces that are part of the hierarchy * between type and toClass. So with the above * example, this method will also determine that the type arguments for * {@link java.util.Hashtable Hashtable} are also both Object. * In cases where the interface specified by toClass is * (indirectly) implemented more than once (e.g. where toClass * specifies the interface {@link java.lang.Iterable Iterable} and * type specifies a parameterized type that implements both * {@link java.util.Set Set} and {@link java.util.Collection Collection}), * this method will look at the inheritance hierarchy of only one of the * implementations/subclasses; the first interface encountered that isn't a * subinterface to one of the others in the type to * toClass hierarchy.

* * @param type the type from which to determine the type parameters of * toClass * @param toClass the class whose type parameters are to be determined based * on the subtype type * @return a map of the type assignments for the type variables in each type * in the inheritance hierarchy from type to * toClass inclusive. "

The failing test `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments()` is testing the method `getTypeArguments` from the class `TypeUtils` in Apache Commons Lang3 library. This method is used to get the type arguments of a class/interface based on a subtype. It returns `null` if the given `type` is not assignable to the `toClass`.

The current bug report mentions that the method `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments()` misses type arguments for partially-assigned classes, and it provides a failing test code to reproduce the issue. The failing test code includes a call to `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class)` and asserts the size of the returned map and the type arguments for specific classes.

Based on the description of the `getTypeArguments` method, it iterates through the inheritance hierarchy from the given `type` to the `toClass`, inclusive, to determine the type assignments for the type variables.

To diagnose the issue:
1. The failing test is calling `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class)`, but the expected behavior is not explicitly described. It seems the issue might be related to how the type arguments are resolved for `Other.class` and `This.class`.
2. The implementation of `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type type, Class<?> toClass)` method is responsible for retrieving the type assignments but may not be handling the scenario when dealing with partially-assigned classes correctly.
3. The bug report indicates that there might be a discrepancy in how type arguments are assigned or retrieved for partially-assigned classes, leading to missing type arguments in the result.

To fix the issue, the method `org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect.TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(java.lang.reflect.Type, java.lang.Class<?>)` should be reviewed and updated to handle the scenario of partially-assigned classes correctly.

Best locations to be fixed:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect.TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(java.lang.reflect.Type, java.lang.Class<?>)`
